coverage_notes:
PRIMARY SOURCE: the University of Alabama athletics staff directory (rolltide.com/staff.aspx) archived by the Wayback Machine at 20180109063923 — January 9, 2018, the morning AFTER Alabama beat Georgia 26-23 in the CFP National Championship on January 8, 2018. This is the ideal snapshot for the "on staff at the championship game" ring rule. I verified it is byte-for-byte identical in the FOOTBALL, STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING, TRAINING, EQUIPMENT and VIDEO SERVICES sections to the 20171130125028 (Nov 30, 2017, mid-season) snapshot, so no roster churn occurred in that window. A season-labeled page titled "2017 Football Coaching Staff" (coaches.aspx?path=football, archived 20170828042923) corroborates the ten on-field coaches.

QUOTE FORMAT WARNING — please read before machine-matching. The rolltide.com directory is an HTML table: the person's name sits in a `<th>` cell and the title in a separate adjacent `<td>` cell, with markup between them. There is NO contiguous "Name + Title" string anywhere in that page. So for every person sourced to that directory I set `quote` to the exact Title-cell text, which IS a contiguous verbatim substring of the page, and I put the name-to-row binding in `note` (including the exact name-cell text). Do not expect "Nick Saban Head Coach" to match. Note two literal quirks I preserved: the name cell for Brendan Farrell contains a DOUBLE space ("Brendan  Farrell"), and Terry Jones's title uses a straight apostrophe in "Women's Basketball". Titles such as "Football Analyst" and "Assistant Strength and Conditioning Coach, Football" are shared by several people, so those quotes are verbatim but not individually distinguishing — the `note` field disambiguates. Where a clean contiguous prose sentence existed (Wikipedia bios, 247Sports, Roll 'Bama Roll), I used that instead.

WEBFETCH LIMITATION: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before I started (200/200 used), and WebFetch is blocked from web.archive.org in this environment. All archive work was done with curl, and I extracted quotes from raw HTML rather than a rendered view. Quotes are copied character-for-character from that HTML after entity unescaping.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT / DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS:
1. FREDDIE ROACH — EXCLUDED as an apparent Wikipedia error. The 2017 team article lists him among 2017 analysts, but his own Wikipedia biography says "Roach was recruited to be the defensive line coach for Ole Miss by head coach Hugh Freeze in 2017" and has him at Ole Miss through 2019, returning to Alabama only in 2020. He is also absent from the Wikipedia "2017 Alabama Crimson Tide football—consensus national champions" navbox, and absent from the Jan 2018 rolltide directory. I did not include him rather than pad.
2. JESSE WILLIAMS — EXCLUDED. Roll 'Bama Roll (March 2017) says he "serves as Assistant Coach, Sports Science/Performance," but he does not appear in either the Nov 2017 or Jan 2018 staff directory, so I could not confirm he was on staff at the title game.
3. ATHLETICS-WIDE SUPPORT DEPARTMENTS. Alabama's directory organized sports medicine ("TRAINING"), equipment, and nutrition as athletics-wide units rather than football units. Only Jeremy Gsell carries an explicit football designation ("Assistant Athletic Trainer/Football"). I included the two unit heads — Jeff Allen (Associate Athletics Director, Sports Medicine) and Jeffrey Springer (Associate Athletics Director, Equipment Operations) — flagged in their notes as athletics-wide titles, because both are the responsible leads for football; but I did NOT include the remaining ~18 training-room and equipment names (Rodney Brown, Amy Bragg, Sherry Kimbro, Ginger Gilmore, Kevin Murray, Frank Newell, Amanda Poppleton, Jakob Walden, Garrett Walker, Kyle Smith, Eric Cookmeyer, and the sport-assigned trainers) because the source gives no football-specific attribution. Several of them very likely worked football; I have no evidence to prove it, so they are omitted rather than guessed. Alabama's football support headcount is therefore probably somewhat larger than the 49 rows here.
4. NO MEDIA GUIDE FOUND. I could not locate a 2017 Alabama football media guide PDF on the Wayback Machine (CDX queries for grfx.cstv.com and rolltide.com/documents PDFs returned no 2017 football guide; several regex-filtered CDX queries timed out with 504s). Alabama appears to have stopped publishing a printed football media guide by this era. A media guide would normally add student assistants, interns, and recruiting staff not in the web directory.
5. GRADUATE ASSISTANTS are not listed in the athletics staff directory at all. The three GAs (Mike Miller, Nick Perry, Kyle Pope) come from the Wikipedia team-season article's GA list plus corroborating biography/news sources. There may have been additional GAs — programs typically carry four — that I could not document.
6. Wikipedia's 2017 team article also lists Rob Ezell and Alex Mortensen as analysts; neither appears in the rolltide directory's analyst block, so I sourced them to their own Wikipedia biographies (both explicitly cover 2017 at Alabama, and both appear in the champions navbox). Mortensen's page carries no prose sentence about the role, only the infobox coaching timeline, so his quote is the run-together infobox string "2017–2019Alabama (analyst)" — verbatim from the rendered page but visually odd; a secondary 247Sports quote is included.
7. MIDSEASON NOTES: Jeremy Pruitt was hired as Tennessee's head coach in December 2017 but stayed to coach Alabama's defense through the title game (he is still listed in the Jan 9, 2018 directory). Brian Niedermeyer followed Pruitt to Tennessee as tight ends coach; he is likewise still in the Jan 9, 2018 directory and his Wikipedia infobox credits him with the 2017 CFP title. Both are flagged.
8. Burton Burns's title differs between the two official pages: "Associate Head Coach/Running Backs/Special Teams" (Aug 2017 coaches page) vs "Associate Head Coach/Running Backs" (Jan 2018 directory). I used the January wording and cited both.
